post.title: SSC CGL vs CHSL: Complete Difference Guide — Which Is Better for You?
post.description: Understand the key differences between SSC CGL and SSC CHSL exams including eligibility, salary, posts, difficulty, and career growth to make the right choice.
post.author: GovtExamPath Team
post.body:
## SSC CGL vs CHSL: Understanding the Basics

Both SSC CGL and SSC CHSL are conducted by the Staff Selection Commission and recruit for central government posts. However, they differ significantly in eligibility, post levels, salary, and career trajectory. Choosing the right one depends on your qualifications and career goals.

## Eligibility Comparison

| Criteria | SSC CGL | SSC CHSL |
|----------|---------|----------|
| **Minimum Education** | Bachelor's Degree (Graduation) | 12th Pass (Intermediate) |
| **Age Limit (General)** | 18-32 years | 18-27 years |
| **Age Relaxation (OBC)** | +3 years | +3 years |
| **Age Relaxation (SC/ST)** | +5 years | +5 years |

**Key Point:** If you have a graduation degree, you can apply for both CGL and CHSL. Many graduates take CHSL as a backup while preparing for CGL.

## Posts and Pay Levels

### SSC CGL Posts (Group B & C)
| Post | Pay Level | Basic Pay | Department |
|------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Inspector (Income Tax) | Level 7 | Rs 44,900 | CBDT |
| Inspector (Customs/Excise) | Level 7 | Rs 44,900 | CBIC |
| Assistant Section Officer | Level 6 | Rs 35,400 | CSS/MEA |
| Sub-Inspector (CBI) | Level 6 | Rs 35,400 | CBI |
| Tax Assistant | Level 4 | Rs 25,500 | CBDT/CBIC |
| Auditor | Level 5 | Rs 29,200 | CAG/CGDA |

### SSC CHSL Posts (Group C)
| Post | Pay Level | Basic Pay | Department |
|------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Lower Division Clerk (LDC) | Level 2 | Rs 19,900 | Various Ministries |
| Junior Secretariat Assistant | Level 2 | Rs 19,900 | Various |
| Data Entry Operator | Level 4 | Rs 25,500 | Various |
| Postal Assistant / Sorting Assistant | Level 4 | Rs 25,500 | Dept. of Posts |

## Salary Comparison (In-Hand Monthly)

| Component | SSC CGL (Tax Asst.) | SSC CGL (Inspector) | SSC CHSL (LDC) |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| Basic Pay | Rs 25,500 | Rs 44,900 | Rs 19,900 |
| DA (50%) | Rs 12,750 | Rs 22,450 | Rs 9,950 |
| HRA (27% metro) | Rs 6,885 | Rs 12,123 | Rs 5,373 |
| TA | Rs 3,600 | Rs 7,200 | Rs 3,600 |
| **Total (approx.)** | **Rs 48,000** | **Rs 86,000** | **Rs 38,000** |

## Exam Pattern Comparison

### SSC CGL
- **Tier I:** 100 questions, 200 marks, 60 minutes (GI, GK, Quant, English)
- **Tier II:** Session I (390 marks) + Session II (module-based, 200 marks)
- **Total stages:** 2 computer-based tests
- **Difficulty:** Moderate to high, especially Tier II mathematics

### SSC CHSL
- **Tier I:** 100 questions, 200 marks, 60 minutes (same subjects as CGL)
- **Tier II:** Descriptive paper — Essay (200-250 words) + Letter/Application (150-200 words), 100 marks, 60 minutes
- **Tier III:** Skill/Typing test (qualifying)
- **Difficulty:** Easy to moderate. Tier I level is lower than CGL

## Difficulty Analysis

SSC CGL is harder because:
- Tier II has advanced mathematics (Geometry, Algebra, Trigonometry, Statistics)
- Competition is higher with 30+ lakh applicants
- Questions are more analytical and conceptually deep
- Cut-offs are higher relative to the difficulty

SSC CHSL is comparatively easier because:
- Questions are based on 10+2 level knowledge
- Tier II is descriptive (essay + letter) — easier to prepare
- Cut-offs are lower
- More vacancies relative to applicants

## Career Growth

### SSC CGL Path
- Tax Assistant to Income Tax Officer (10-15 years)
- Inspector to Assistant Commissioner (15-20 years)
- ASO to Under Secretary (15 years)
- **Promotion to Group A is possible** for top posts

### SSC CHSL Path
- LDC to UDC (5-8 years based on seniority)
- UDC to Assistant/Head Clerk (10-15 years)
- Limited upward mobility — highest typical level is Section Officer
- **Promotion beyond Group C is rare** without further exams

## Who Should Choose SSC CGL?

- You have a graduation degree
- You want a higher starting salary (Rs 45,000-85,000/month)
- You aim for Group B officer-level posts
- You're willing to invest 6-12 months in intensive preparation
- Career growth and promotion prospects matter to you

## Who Should Choose SSC CHSL?

- You've completed 12th and want a government job quickly
- You want a secure job while pursuing higher education
- You prefer a descriptive exam over advanced mathematics
- You want to gain government experience early (typing/clerical)
- You plan to prepare for CGL later while working in CHSL post

## Can You Prepare for Both Simultaneously?

Yes, and this is the recommended approach if you're a graduate:

1. **Prepare at CGL level** — CHSL Tier I becomes easy automatically
2. **Take CHSL as a safety net** — The exam is usually held before CGL
3. **Focus on descriptive writing** for CHSL Tier II separately
4. **Practice typing** (35 WPM English / 30 WPM Hindi) for CHSL skill test

## The Verdict

If you're a graduate with time to prepare, always aim for SSC CGL first — the salary, perks, and growth are significantly better. Use CHSL as a backup. If you've completed 12th and need a job quickly, CHSL is an excellent entry point into government service, and you can always appear for CGL later while working.
